Hi Jordan / Healix security team — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the two items we agreed we'd deliver: 

1) Example "who-viewed-when" export (sample CSV) showing the minimal set you need for compliance review and e-discovery.
2) Export schema and delivery options (S3 push vs. secure Drive link), retention toggles, and pseudonymization/PII minimization modes.

Notes from the call: Healix wants: a) per-event actor identifier (user id or service id), b) action verb (view/create/delete), c) resource identifier (document id / record path), d) precise UTC timestamp, e) model/request id for inference calls, and f) proof that logs are immutable for 90 days. You also flagged that exported data must either omit plaintext user PII or pseudonymize the actor field depending on the dataset.

Next steps from Redwood (this thread):
- I'll attach a one-page CSV sample (columns + example rows) and the JSON export schema.
- Karthik will confirm which fields we can redaction-mask automatically vs. which require Healix to self-redact before ingest.
- Jordan / Mark: please confirm whether you need timestamps in millisecond epoch or ISO-8601 UTC, and whether session_id is required.

Attachments: healix_who_viewed_when_sample.csv (stub) and redwood_audit_export_schema_v1.json (schema).

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the fast recap. A few clarifications from Healix Security so Karthik can scope the export: 

- Timestamp format: we prefer ISO-8601 UTC (e.g., 2027-02-15T14:34:00Z). Millis are optional but useful for correlation; if you can include both that'd be ideal.
- Actor identifier: must be pseudonymizable. We cannot receive raw emails or employee PII in exports — hashed user_id is OK if you provide the hashing algorithm and salt management approach.
- Resource identifier: must include a human-readable path plus an internal ID for linking to our audit system.
- Immutability: we need evidence (write-once export or signed manifest) proving the export hasn't been altered after generation.
- Retention: export retention policy for our account: 365 days (we may request longer later).

Also, can Redwood provide a 10-row sample with one inference event and one admin-view event so our compliance team can confirm field coverage? If you can push the sample to an S3 link with presigned URL, send it encrypted and we'll retrieve it.

Jordan Lee
Security Operations Lead, Healix Health
jordan.lee@healix.com

Priyom / Monica — quick technical note (so Jordan knows what to expect):

We can emit an export that includes the fields Healix requested. Proposed column set (CSV) and semantics: 
- event_ts_iso (ISO-8601 UTC)
- event_ts_epoch_ms (numeric) — optional, for correlation
- actor_id_hashed (sha256 hex) — Redwood can hash with per-customer salt; we can provide proof-of-salt via HSM-based key reference on request
- actor_role (user | admin | service)
- action (view | generate | delete | update)
- resource_id (opaque UUID)
- resource_path (human readable path)
- model_id (string)
- request_id (redwood request uuid)
- session_id (optional)
- retention_flag (exported_retention_days)

On immutability: we can produce a signed manifest (SHA256 of CSV + timestamp + export metadata) and store manifests in an append-only ledger for 90 days. For stricter needs we can push to Healix S3 and optionally sign the file via our KMS.

On pseudonymization vs redaction: Redwood can hash actor identifiers. If Healix needs reversible mapping (for internal investigations), we can offer a blinded enclave workflow under Private deployment — otherwise hashing is non-reversible and should satisfy privacy constraints.

I'll attach a short schema doc and a 10-row CSV sample (no PII, actor_id hashed).

—Karthik
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Jordan / Mark — attached are the two stubs Karthik mentioned: a 10-row CSV sample (healix_who_viewed_when_sample.csv) and the export schema (redwood_audit_export_schema_v1.json). Notes: 

- Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC in event_ts_iso and we included epoch ms where available.
- actor_id_hashed is sha256(email + customer_salt) — we are including the algorithm note in the schema but not the salt. If Healix wants Redwood to manage reversible mappings, we can discuss Private deployment options.
- Manifest: redwood will provide a signed manifest for each export. We will store manifests for 540 days by default for customers with an SLA, but we can set the manifest retention to match Healix's requested 365-day retention.
- Delivery: we can do a presigned S3 push (AES-256 encrypted in transit + at rest) or a secured Drive link; your preference.

Actions for Healix: 
- Reply here with preferred delivery method (S3 presigned push OR secured Drive link).
- Confirm session_id inclusion. If you confirm, we'll include session_id column in the export.
- Confirm that hashed actor_id is acceptable for your compliance review; if not, call out whether you need reversible mapping and we can scope a Private deployment add-on.

If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow with Karthik to walk the security team through the sample.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation so we can generate a live sample export to your S3.
